Let
\[
q(t)=(1-\beta t)(1-\alpha t)=1-(\alpha+\beta)t+\alpha\beta t^2.
\]
For \(J_\lambda=\lambda I+N\), \(N^2=0\),
\[
E_{\alpha,\beta}(J_\lambda)=q(\lambda)I+q'(\lambda)N
=
\begin{bmatrix}
a&b\\0&a
\end{bmatrix},
\]
where \(a=q(\lambda)\), \(b=q'(\lambda)\).

A useful exact norm criterion is:
\[
\left\|\begin{bmatrix}a&b\\0&a\end{bmatrix}\right\|_2\le r
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
a^2+r|b|\le r^2.
\]
This follows by checking positive semidefiniteness of \(r^2I-T^TT\).

Write
\[
A=q(1),\quad U=q'(1),\quad B=q(4),\quad V=q'(4).
\]
For every quadratic \(q(t)=1-st+pt^2\),
\[
1=\frac{16}{17}A-\frac{64}{51}U+\frac1{17}B+\frac4{51}V.
\]
If both endpoint norms are at most \(r\), then the norm criterion and the elementary support bounds
\[
\frac34 a-b\le \frac{73}{64},\qquad \frac34 a+b\le \frac{73}{64}
\]
on \(a^2+|b|\le 1\) give
\[
1\le r\left(\frac{73}{51}+\frac{73}{816}\right)=r\frac{73}{48}.
\]
Hence
\[
\rho(\alpha,\beta)\ge \frac{48}{73}.
\]

Equality forces
\[
q(1)=q(4)=\frac{18}{73},\qquad q'(1)=-\frac{165}{292},\qquad q'(4)=\frac{165}{292}.
\]
Thus, with \(s=\alpha+\beta\), \(p=\alpha\beta\),
\[
s=5p,\qquad 1-4p=\frac{18}{73},
\]
so
\[
p=\frac{55}{292},\qquad s=\frac{275}{292}.
\]
Therefore \(\alpha,\beta\) are the roots of
\[
x^2-\frac{275}{292}x+\frac{55}{292}=0,
\]
namely
\[
\alpha_*=\frac{275-3\sqrt{1265}}{584},\qquad
\beta_*=\frac{275+3\sqrt{1265}}{584}.
\]
At this pair both endpoint norms equal \(48/73\), so the minimum contraction factor is
\[
\frac{48}{73}.
\]

Final answer:
\[
\boxed{\left(\frac{275-3\sqrt{1265}}{584},\frac{275+3\sqrt{1265}}{584}\right)}.
\]
